title: Unbounded strong-product ratios for the Grundy domination number
journal: Journal of Combinatorial Theory, Series B

abstract_tex: We prove that the ratio of the Grundy domination number of a strong product to the product of the Grundy domination numbers of its factors is unbounded over nonempty finite graphs. For each integer $m\ge5$, we construct two graphs on the five-element subsets of an $m$-element set. Their Grundy domination numbers are at most $m$ and $\binom m2$, whereas their strong product has an independent set of size $\binom m5$. Incidence matrices over two finite fields give a self-contained proof. We also determine the Grundy domination number of the graph on $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ with adjacency $|u-v|\equiv2\pmod3$: it is $\lfloor(N+1)/3\rfloor+3$ for every $N\ge6$. An explicit legal sequence in its product with the octahedron gives a counterexample on $114$ vertices to the strong-product multiplicativity conjecture. Both general results have elementary proofs independent of computation. A separate Lean certificate concerns one finite example.

For each integer m>=5, we construct two graphs on the five-element subsets of an m-element set. Their Grundy domination numbers are at most m and binomial m2, whereas their strong product has an independent set of size binomial m5. Incidence matrices over two finite fields give a self-contained proof. We also determine the Grundy domination number of the graph on 0,ldots,N-1 with adjacency |u-v|equiv2pmod3: it is floor((N+1)/3)+3 for every N>=6. An explicit legal sequence in its product with the octahedron gives a counterexample on 114 vertices to the strong-product multiplicativity conjecture. Both general results have elementary proofs independent of computation. A separate Lean certificate concerns one finite example.
